newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris Bourse suspends trading in Russian bonds.
newsitem.headline: Paris Bourse suspends trading in Russian bonds.

text.p: The French Stock Markets' association SBF said it had decided to suspend trading in Russian bonds from today.

"Because of rumours that have been relayed by verious information services, relative to Russian bonds, the listing of these is provisionally suspended from today, November 25, 1996," the SBF said in a statement.
The bonds listed in Paris are from the Tsarist era.

Russia on Thursday returned to the international financial markets with a $1.0 billion five-year Eurobond and there have been rumours in Paris that Russia would make some kind of compensation payment to the holders of the old bonds.
Russia has defaulted on its loans since the Communist took power in 1917. Before that there had been close financial ties between Russia and France.
The loans were used to finance the Transsiberian railroad and other big projects. The successors of the original buyers of the bonds are claiming back some $30 billion, newspapers reported.
On October 29, Russian newsagency Itar-Tass quoted Finance Minister Alexandre Livchits as saying that French and Russian negotiators were close to agreement of a "symbolic" gesture.
Russian Prime Minister Victor Tchernomyrdine will be on an official vist to France on November 26 and 27.

"There have been negotiations for many years. We hope that they will finally be completed so that French savers can again respond to the financing needs of the Russian state," a spokesman for the Foreign Affairs ministry said on Friday.
